title: ClickKart — Platform Health
description: Built around the failures this platform has actually had, not around whatever Micrometer happens to expose. Every panel earns its place by corresponding to something that has gone wrong or plausibly will.

panels.title: Services up
panels.description: A service that is registered in Eureka but not answering a scrape is still down. This counts what actually responds.

panels.title: HikariCP — active connections per service
panels.description: The metric that would have caught the real incident: 10 services x a default pool of 10 exceeds Postgres's default max_connections of 100, and the first symptom was psql itself being refused. Watch this against max_connections, not against zero.

panels.title: Total DB connections held
panels.description: Sum across every pool. Postgres defaults to max_connections=100; crossing it does not degrade gracefully, it refuses new connections outright.

panels.title: 5xx responses per second
panels.description: Server-side failures only. 4xx is deliberately excluded: on this platform a 409 is usually a correct business answer - a customer losing the race for the last unit - and counting those as errors would bury real faults under normal checkout traffic.

panels.title: Request latency — p95
panels.description: p95 rather than mean. Checkout fans out to User, then Product per line, then Inventory per line, so its tail is where a slow downstream service shows up first - and a mean would hide it.

panels.title: JVM heap used
panels.description: The Docker VM here is under 4 GB and has been OOM-killed by the full stack more than once. This is where that becomes visible before a container exits 137.

panels.title: Request rate by outcome
panels.description: Splitting by outcome rather than plotting a single total: the shape of a spike matters more than its height. A rise in CLIENT_ERROR alongside flat SUCCESS is a client that has started sending something wrong, which reads nothing like an outage.
